title: Congo Starts Ebola Vaccines for Health Workers in Outbreak Center
summary:
Health workers in Congo are first in line for an Ebola vaccine. On Saturday, the country started vaccinating them in Bunia, the city at the center of the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

Ebola is a serious disease that can spread from person to person. This outbreak is caused by a type called Bundibugyo virus. There is no licensed vaccine or treatment for that type yet.

So why use a vaccine? The vaccine, called Ervebo, is approved for a different, more common type of Ebola. Scientists think it might offer some protection because the two viruses are related. They are studying whether it actually works against Bundibugyo.

Front-line workers are being prioritized because they are "particularly exposed and deeply involved in the response," said Maj. Gen. Gaby Kasongo Mulumba, the military governor of Ituri province. The campaign is expected to cover 20,000 workers over six to nine months.

As of Saturday, Congo had recorded 7,541 confirmed cases and 3,639 deaths. The outbreak is the deadliest of the country's 17 Ebola outbreaks. The World Health Organization says it is still out of control and could surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak, which killed more than 11,000 people.

Dr. Jeannot Elua, a health worker in Bunia, said the vaccine is "beneficial." "We healthcare workers don't really have a choice: we are going to receive it," he said.
why_it_matters: It shows why countries move fast when a dangerous disease spreads, and why the people who care for the sick are protected first — the same idea behind the shots kids get to stay healthy.

background_read: Ebola is named after the Ebola River in central Africa, where scientists first identified the virus in 1976. It spreads when someone touches the body fluids of a sick person.
Congo (officially the Democratic Republic of the Congo — a large country in central Africa) has had many Ebola outbreaks before this one.

During a big Ebola outbreak in Congo, health workers were vaccinated first with the same kind of shot being used now. The World Health Organization (a group that works to keep people around the world healthy) helps countries respond to outbreaks like this.

WHERE: In Bunia, the city at the center of the outbreak, in Ituri province in Congo.
WHY: Front-line workers are the most exposed to the virus, and this is the deadliest of Congo's 17 Ebola outbreaks and is still out of control.
